The required synthesizable top module is adaptive_aero_control_top. Do not substitute a status, telemetry, register-bank, or leaf module as the design top. The top must implement the selected Physical AI application contract, external model request/response transport, validation, safety, timeout, fallback, and bounded actuator-command behavior.

EXTERNAL MODEL TRANSPORT DIRECTION CONTRACT (mandatory; this takes precedence over ambiguous ingress/egress wording in upstream prose): the RTL emits model-request valid/data as outputs and receives model-request ready as an input. The RTL receives model-response valid/data as inputs and emits model-response ready as an output. Apply this rule by data flow even when application-specific ports use cmd_*, req_*, rsp_*, or response_* names. A top-level output must have a real RTL driver; never connect a required top-level output only to a child input.

FIRMWARE CONTROL-PLANE CONTRACT (mandatory): this product journey requests generated firmware. The synthesizable top must expose a real firmware-visible CSR/MMIO interface with address, write-data, read-data, transaction-valid/write-enable, and response/ready semantics. DIGITAL_SPEC_JSON.register_contract must describe the implemented registers and fields. Every declared register must be reachable through RTL decode; do not label inaccessible internal state as software-visible. The streaming transport may coexist with, but cannot replace, this interface.

The application RTL must expose the selected bus and MMIO interface. Do not claim the CPU is instantiated or board-ready until its RTL, memory/interconnect, and application RTL are synthesized and routed together.
Design a synthesizable FPGA digital IP top module named adaptive_aero_control_top for an intelligent active-aerodynamics controller. The design shall target a PicoRV32 soft CPU subsystem running on Wishbone at 50 MHz and shall not implement the NVIDIA DoMINO surrogate in RTL. The RTL top level shall expose only a compact control/status interface and actuator interface; it shall not expose vehicle geometry arrays, pressure fields, flow fields, or any surrogate tensor payloads at top level.

Top-level ports shall include a 32-bit Wishbone slave/control window wb_ctrl, a 1-bit irq_out, a 32-bit actuator_cmd_out, 1-bit actuator_valid, 1-bit actuator_ready, 1-bit fault_in, and optional 1-bit uart_tx/uart_rx. The Wishbone window shall decode a small fixed register map, implemented with flip-flops for control/status and no more than a few dozen registers. All bulk model-state information shall remain in software or external memory managed by the soft CPU; the RTL shall only store small control words, timestamps, and flags.

Required register behavior:
- REG0 control: enable, clear_fault, fallback_override, model_source_select, reserved.
- REG1 status: active_state, fault_latched, stale_data_flag, timeout_flag, clamp_applied, ready_flag.
- REG2 command_setpoint: normalized actuator target and mode bits.
- REG3 limit_config: programmable min/max limits for clamp logic.
- REG4 timeout_config: stale-data threshold in timebase ticks.
- REG5 timestamp: sampled free-running counter low bits for software correlation.
- REG6 irq_mask and irq_status.
All unused bits shall read as zero and writes to reserved fields shall be ignored.

Implement a free-running timestamp_counter used for command freshness and watchdog timing. The command_safety_guard shall compare the current timestamp against the stored command timestamp. If the age exceeds timeout_config, the stale_data_detector shall assert stale_data_flag, deassert actuator_valid, and force safe_fallback_fsm into the safe state. The safe state shall drive a predefined benign actuator command corresponding to minimal aerodynamic actuation or hold-last-safe value, as configured by firmware, but shall never exceed limits.

Implement actuator_command_clamper as purely combinational or registered datapath logic that saturates the command setpoint to the programmed min/max range. If clamping occurs, clamp_applied shall be set until cleared by software or reset. The output actuator_cmd_out shall present the clamped command word in a deterministic format documented by the register map; actuator_valid shall only assert when enable is set, no fault is latched, command age is within threshold, and downstream actuator_ready is asserted or the command is being held in a one-deep valid/ready staging register.

Implement a one-deep staging register for actuator commands only; this is a control word, not a payload FIFO. The staging register shall capture a validated command when actuator_ready is low and hold it until accepted, while maintaining stale-data checks against the original timestamp. Do not implement unbounded FIFOs or register-array payload memories for model data.

Safe fallback behavior shall be deterministic and priority encoded above normal control. Conditions that must trigger fallback are: reset, fault_in high, timeout expiry, stale_data detection, invalid command encoding, or explicit clear_fault absence after a latched fault. In fallback, actuator_valid shall deassert or only assert with the safe command if the downstream interface requires a valid beat, and actuator_cmd_out shall present the configured safe command. The safe_fallback_fsm shall provide active_state encoding and status flags.

Interrupt logic shall raise irq_out when any enabled status transition occurs: new valid command accepted, stale data detected, timeout, fault latched, or fallback entered. irq_status shall be sticky until software writes a one to clear the corresponding bit. irq_mask shall enable per-event interrupt generation.

Bus timing and synthesis requirements: all sequential logic shall use a single clock domain unless the UART is internally synchronized. Reset shall be synchronous or synchronized-deasserted. No inferred latches. No combinational loops. All state elements shall have defined reset values. The design shall be fully synthesizable for FPGA implementation using standard flip-flops, LUTs, and FPGA block RAM only if a small command-history buffer is needed for debug; any such buffer shall remain bounded and shall not store surrogate tensors or geometry payloads.

Firmware/software partitioning requirement: the soft CPU is responsible for loading geometry metadata, managing CPU-reference execution, polling or interrupt-driven collection of model/reference outputs from external software, and writing validated actuator setpoints into the Wishbone register window. The RTL shall not call the surrogate model or encode its input/output tensors. Instead, it shall provide deterministic transport, validation, timeout handling, and actuator command acceptance.

Timing/safety constraints: stale-data timeout must be programmable and enforced in hardware. The design shall reject any command older than the configured threshold. Actuator command clamping shall be enforced even if firmware misconfigures setpoints. Fallback shall be immediate upon hard fault. The default post-reset state shall be safe and disabled. All scalar outputs shall be initialized to safe values.

Implementation constraints: the RTL top shall keep estimated scalar-equivalent I/O count below 256. The interface shall remain implementation-friendly for FPGA soft CPU integration. Do not instantiate Sky130 ASIC hard macros or ASIC-only memories in the FPGA path. Do not expose the DoMINO model interface as a top-level hardware data path.
FPGA MEMORY CONTRACT (mandatory): describe bulk payload/history/FIFO storage through a technology-neutral memory wrapper that the FPGA flow can map to native block RAM; do not flatten it into registers.
